newsitem.title: SWEDEN: S&P removes Sydkraft, Vattenfall from creditwatch.
newsitem.headline: S&P removes Sydkraft, Vattenfall from creditwatch.

text.p: U.S. credit ratings agency Standard & Poor's (S&P) said on Thursday it had removed Swedish power companies Sydkraft AB and state-owned Vattenfall AB from creditwatch.
It affirmed both companies ratings which were reassessed in light of the Swedish government's decision to start phasing out nuclear power.
In a statement S&P said it affirmed Sydkraft's long-term issuer credit rating of AA-, its short-term issuer credit rating of A-1+ and its commercial credit rating of A-1+.
The outlook for Sydkraft remained negative.
"(This) reflects that the changing structure of Sweden's electricity generation with the phase-out of nuclear power, at some point, could affect the company's financial profile," S&P said.
It affirmed Sydkraft's commercial paper rating at K-1.

Sydkraft, which is Sweden's second largest producer and distributor of electricity, wholly owns the first of Sweden's 12 nuclear reactors that is to be closed in July 1998. This is located at Barseback on Sweden's west coast.
A second reactor at Barseback was due to close in 2001 under the government's plans to phase out nuclear power.
S&P affirmed Vattenfall AB's AA long-term issuer credit rating and Vattenfall AB/Vattenfall Treasury AB ratings of A-1+ for short-term issuer credit and K-1/A-1+ for Swedish commercial paper.
Vattenfall Treasury Inc's commercial paper rating was affirmed at A-1+.

"These ratings will continue to be supported by Vattenfall's strong position as the largest generator and supplier of electricity in the Nordic countries as well as its stable income from regional grid and local network operations and heat supply," S&P said.
S&P said Vattenfall's financial position was not expected to be significantly affected by the upcoming changes in the Swedish electricity industry.

"The creditwatch placement reflected uncertainties regarding Vattenfall's role in the process of transforming the Swedish electrical sector from reliance on nuclear power based production to the use of other sources as energy," S&P said.
Sydkraft and Vattenfall were placed on creditwatch on January 15, 1997 and February 6, 1997, respectively.
